chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, is not a tyrant to His servants, nor distant from them, nor heedless of them, nor cutting off His mercy from them, nor mistaken in His judgment, nor changing from His covenant, nor returning from His promise, nor breaking His word, nor changing His messenger, nor changing His favor, nor changing His state, nor changing His will, nor changing His mercy, nor changing His justice, nor changing His wisdom, nor changing His power, nor changing His might, nor changing His greatness, nor changing His loftiness, nor changing His elevation.
ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah regarding justice and mercy in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to ground the Shia doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*) in Allah’s immutable nature, distinguishing Him from anthropomorphic conceptions of change. This consistency in judgment reinforces the theological certainty that God’s promises and warnings are absolute, providing a foundation for believer's trust (*Tawakkul*) and accountability in the hereafter.
